summary: One generic, type-agnostic CRUD store for encrypted account/snapshot/profile records, with server-enforced field consistency, optimistic-concurrency versioning, and a byte-exact client-built AAD the server never sees.

versionRule.value: starts at 1, +1 per write; PUT must supply stored version + 1 (or 1 to create)

aadEncoding.value: each field UTF-8 text; account_id empty is empty string (not null) and still contributes its separator; schema_version and version are unpadded decimal

accountIdOnWire.value: null when absent, everywhere (PUT body, GET response, export file); empty string is rejected as malformed

endpoints.note: no single-record GET; DELETE /api/accounts/<account_id>?mode=purge is owned by manage-accounts.md, not this contract

fixtures: byte-exact AAD fixture for a known (account_id, record_type, record_id, schema_version, version) tuple, including the empty-account_id case
two seeded users each with records of all three types, for cross-user isolation and 404-not-403 tests
a record stored at an older schema_version, to assert reads leave version/nonce/ciphertext byte-identical
a record at a schema_version above the client's known version, to assert it is skipped and counted rather than guessed at
focus: 409 responses must leave the stored row byte-identical, not just return the right status
a rejected write (400/409/413) must not increment version or write anything — easy to fake by only checking the response code
the AAD assertion must be byte-for-byte against the fixture, including separators, not just 'contains the right substrings'
no log line contains a ciphertext value — requires inspecting actual log output, not just the response
a userId or aad field in the request body must be rejected outright, not silently stripped and ignored
